title: Products of bases form a basis in a tower
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $M$ an $S$-module, regarded also as an $R$-module through $R\to S$. Let $(\beta_j)_{j\in J}$ be a basis of $S$ as an $R$-module and $(\alpha_i)_{i\in I}$ a basis of $M$ as an $S$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Then the family $(\beta_j\alpha_i)_{(j,i)\in J\times I}$ is a basis of $M$ as an $R$-module. (In particular, for fields $k\subseteq E\subseteq F$ [def-pc-field-extension], a $k$-basis of $E$ times an $E$-basis of $F$ is a $k$-basis of $F$.)
